note: GCSE track (Year 11) for Gan Ainm, drafted by Claude in Ulster Irish for Dáithí Murray's sign-off. Same builder format as year8.json plus a question chain (qrows maps each question to the rows that answer it), pattern boxes ([ ] marks the letters that change), a basic/better/best ladder ([ ] marks the new words) and role plays.

builders.title: Mé féin agus mo theaghlach
builders.teaches: Introducing yourself and your family; mo + séimhiú (mo dheartháir, mo theaghlach) and m' before a vowel (m'athair); beirt with no séimhiú on d, t, s (beirt deartháireacha); comparing with níos sine / níos óige; giving a reason with mar; Deir mo chairde go bhfuil mé ...

sprioc.ga: Tá mé ag foghlaim le mé féin agus mo theaghlach a chur in aithne.
sprioc.en: I am learning to introduce myself and my family.

sprioc.ga: Tá mé ag foghlaim le barúil a thabhairt agus fáth a lua.
sprioc.en: I am learning to give an opinion and a reason.

patterns.title: Mo agus séimhiú
patterns.question: Cad é a tharlaíonn don fhocal i ndiaidh mo? Cad chuige nach n-athraíonn leabhar ná athair ar an dóigh chéanna?
patterns.questionEn: What happens to the word after mo? Why do leabhar and athair not change in the same way?
patterns.rule: Mo puts a h after the first letter (séimhiú): mo dheartháir. L, n and r never take h: mo leabhar. Before a vowel, mo becomes m': m'athair.

builders.title: Laethanta saoire
builders.teaches: Talking about last summer's holiday in the past tense, with muid for we (chuaigh muid, chaith muid); go dtí + the article, go + a place name; ar an + séimhiú (ar an bhád) and i + urú (i bpuball); weather graded from go hálainn to go holc; a reason with mar; the future for next summer (rachaidh muid).

sprioc.ga: Tá mé ag foghlaim le labhairt faoi mo laethanta saoire san aimsir chaite.
sprioc.en: I am learning to talk about my holidays in the past tense.

sprioc.ga: Tá mé ag foghlaim le freagra bunúsach a fheabhsú.

patterns.title: I agus urú
patterns.question: Cad chuige a n-athraíonn an litriú i gcuid acu ach nach n-athraíonn sé i gcuid eile?
patterns.questionEn: Why does the spelling change in some of them but not in others?
patterns.rule: I eclipses the next word: i bpuball, i gcarbhán. Before a vowel, i becomes in: in óstán. L, m, n, r and s do not change.

patterns.title: Ar an agus séimhiú
patterns.question: Cad é a tharlaíonn i ndiaidh ar an i gcanúint Uladh?
patterns.questionEn: What happens after ar an in Ulster Irish?
patterns.rule: In Ulster, ar an puts a h on the next word: ar an bhád, ar an bhus. T, d and vowels do not change: ar an traein, ar an eitleán.

builders.title: Mo cheantar
builders.teaches: Saying where you live with i + urú (i bPort an Dúnáin, i gCamloch) and sa + séimhiú (sa bhaile mór, sa pháirc) or t before s (sa tSruthán); saying what there is and is not in your area (Tá ... ann, Ach níl ... ann); giving an opinion with a reason (mar); saying what you would change (Ba mhaith liom go mbeadh ..., Bheadh sé deas dá mbeadh ...); the past with An Satharn seo caite.

patterns.title: I agus urú le logainmneacha
patterns.question: Cad é a tharlaíonn d'ainm na háite i ndiaidh i? Cad chuige nach n-athraíonn Ard Mhacha ná Londain ar an dóigh chéanna?
patterns.questionEn: What happens to the place name after i? Why do Ard Mhacha and Londain not change in the same way?
patterns.rule: I eclipses the next word: i mBéal Feirste, i gCamloch, i nDoire. Before a vowel, i becomes in: in Ard Mhacha. L, m, n, r and s do not change: i Londain.
patterns.ruleEn: I eclipses the next word: i mBéal Feirste, i gCamloch, i nDoire. Before a vowel, i becomes in: in Ard Mhacha. L, m, n, r and s do not change: i Londain.

patterns.title: Sa agus séimhiú
patterns.question: Cad é a tharlaíonn i ndiaidh sa? Cad chuige a bhfuil t roimh siopa agus sráid, ach nach n-athraíonn teach?
patterns.questionEn: What happens after sa? Why is there a t before siopa and sráid, but teach does not change?
patterns.rule: Sa means in the. It puts a h after b, c, g, m and p: sa bhaile mór, sa pháirc. Before f, sa becomes san and the f takes a h: san fharraige. Before s followed by a vowel, l, n or r, sa puts a t in front: sa tsiopa, sa tsráid. D and t do not change: sa teach. Before a vowel, sa becomes san: san ionad spóirt.
patterns.ruleEn: Sa means in the. It puts a h after b, c, g, m and p: sa bhaile mór, sa pháirc. Before f, sa becomes san and the f takes a h: san fharraige. Before s followed by a vowel, l, n or r, sa puts a t in front: sa tsiopa, sa tsráid. D and t do not change: sa teach. Before a vowel, sa becomes san: san ionad spóirt.

ladder.en: I live in Lurgan, near Craigavon. It is a big, busy place and there is a swimming pool and a big park in the town. I like my area because there is plenty to do there.
ladder.label: Níos fearr

ladder.ga: Tá mé i mo chónaí sa Lorgain, in aice le Craigavon. Is áit mhór ghnóthach í agus tá linn snámha agus páirc mhór sa bhaile mór. Is maith liom mo cheantar mar tá go leor le déanamh ann. [Ach caithfidh mé a rá nach bhfuil pictiúrlann sa bhaile mór. Dá mbeadh an rogha agam, chuirfinn club óige ar bun, mar níl mórán le déanamh ag daoine óga san oíche.]
ladder.en: I live in Lurgan, near Craigavon. It is a big, busy place and there is a swimming pool and a big park in the town. I like my area because there is plenty to do there. But I have to say that there is no cinema in the town. If I had the choice, I would set up a youth club, because there is not much for young people to do at night.

patterns.title: An aimsir chaite agus séimhiú
patterns.question: Cad é a tharlaíonn don bhriathar san aimsir chaite? Cad chuige a bhfuil d' roimh chuid acu? Cad é atá aisteach faoi téim?
patterns.questionEn: What happens to the verb in the past tense? Why do some of them have d' in front? What is strange about téim?
patterns.rule: In the past tense, put a h after the first letter: bhuail mé, cheannaigh mé. Before a vowel, put d' in front: d'imir mé, d'éirigh mé. F takes both: d'fhan mé. L, n and r do not change: léigh mé. Téigh is irregular: téim becomes chuaigh mé.
patterns.ruleEn: In the past tense, put a h after the first letter: bhuail mé, cheannaigh mé. Before a vowel, put d' in front: d'imir mé, d'éirigh mé. F takes both: d'fhan mé. L, n and r do not change: léigh mé. Téigh is irregular: téim becomes chuaigh mé.

patterns.title: Is maith liom agus ba mhaith liom
patterns.question: Cad é an difear idir is maith liom agus ba mhaith liom? Cad é a tharlaíonn do maith i ndiaidh ba?
patterns.questionEn: What is the difference between is maith liom and ba mhaith liom? What happens to maith after ba?
rows: {Ba} m[h]aith liom an giotár a fhoghlaim.
patterns.rule: Is maith liom means I like, now or in general. Ba mhaith liom means I would like, and an action usually follows it: ba mhaith liom dul ag snámh. Ba puts a h after the next letter: ba mhaith, ba bhreá. Before f or a vowel, ba becomes b': b'fhearr liom. The question and the negative change too: ar mhaith leat? níor mhaith liom.
patterns.ruleEn: Is maith liom means I like, now or in general. Ba mhaith liom means I would like, and an action usually follows it: ba mhaith liom dul ag snámh. Ba puts a h after the next letter: ba mhaith, ba bhreá. Before f or a vowel, ba becomes b': b'fhearr liom. The question and the negative change too: ar mhaith leat? níor mhaith liom.

ladder.ga: Imrím peil Ghaelach. Is maith liom spórt. Inné, d'imir mé peil i ndiaidh na scoile.
ladder.en: I play Gaelic football. I like sport. Yesterday, I played football after school.
ladder.label: Bunúsach

ladder.ga: Imrím peil Ghaelach[ le mo chlub áitiúil dhá uair sa tseachtain]. Is maith liom spórt[ mar bíonn an chraic go maith le mo chairde]. Inné, d'imir mé peil i ndiaidh na scoile[ agus ina dhiaidh sin, bhuail mé le mo chairde sa bhaile mór].
ladder.en: I play Gaelic football with my local club twice a week. I like sport because the craic is good with my friends. Yesterday, I played football after school and after that, I met my friends in town.
ladder.label: Níos fearr

ladder.ga: Imrím peil Ghaelach le mo chlub áitiúil dhá uair sa tseachtain. Is maith liom spórt mar bíonn an chraic go maith le mo chairde. Inné, d'imir mé peil i ndiaidh na scoile agus ina dhiaidh sin, bhuail mé le mo chairde sa bhaile mór. [Caithfidh mé a rá go gcaithim an iomarca ama ar mo ghuthán san oíche, áfach. An deireadh seachtaine seo chugainn, ba mhaith liom dul ag siúl ar Shliabh gCuillinn in áit a bheith istigh os comhair an scáileáin.]
ladder.en: I play Gaelic football with my local club twice a week. I like sport because the craic is good with my friends. Yesterday, I played football after school and after that, I met my friends in town. I have to say that I spend too much time on my phone at night, however. Next weekend, I would like to go walking on Slieve Gullion instead of being inside in front of the screen.

builders.title: Siopadóireacht agus éadaí
builders.teaches: Describing what you wear and your school uniform; colours after the noun, with séimhiú after a feminine noun (léine bhán, casóg dhubh) and no change after a masculine noun (geansaí bán, bríste dubh); numbers with punt (trí phunt, deich bpunt, fiche punt); an opinion with Sílim go bhfuil and the incidental Caithfidh mé a rá go gcuireann ... isteach orm; the past for what you bought (cheannaigh mé, chosain sé); ar + séimhiú (ar chluichí ríomhaire); the future for next weekend (rachaidh mé, ceannóidh mé); asking for things in a shop with de dhíth orm and Cá mhéad atá air?

patterns.title: Uimhreacha agus punt
patterns.question: Cad é a tharlaíonn don fhocal punt i ndiaidh trí, cúig, seacht agus deich? Cad chuige nach n-athraíonn sé i ndiaidh fiche?
patterns.questionEn: What happens to the word punt after three, five, seven and ten? Why does it not change after twenty?
patterns.rule: After 2 to 6 the noun takes a h (séimhiú): trí phunt, cúig phunt. After 7 to 10 it is eclipsed (urú): seacht bpunt, deich bpunt. After fiche, tríocha, caoga and the other tens it does not change: fiche punt. The noun stays singular after a number.
patterns.ruleEn: After 2 to 6 the noun takes a h (séimhiú): trí phunt, cúig phunt. After 7 to 10 it is eclipsed (urú): seacht bpunt, deich bpunt. After fiche, tríocha, caoga and the other tens it does not change: fiche punt. The noun stays singular after a number.

patterns.title: Dathanna i ndiaidh an ainmfhocail
patterns.question: Cad chuige a gcuirtear h ar an fhocal bán i ndiaidh léine ach nach gcuirtear i ndiaidh geansaí? Cad chuige nach n-athraíonn liath?
patterns.questionEn: Why does bán take a h after léine but not after geansaí? Why does liath not change?
patterns.rule: In Irish the colour comes after the noun. After a feminine noun (léine, casóg, T-léine) the colour takes a h (séimhiú): léine bhán, casóg dhubh. After a masculine noun (geansaí, bríste, cóta) it does not change: geansaí bán. L, n and r never take h: casóg liath.
patterns.ruleEn: In Irish the colour comes after the noun. After a feminine noun (léine, casóg, T-léine) the colour takes a h (séimhiú): léine bhán, casóg dhubh. After a masculine noun (geansaí, bríste, cóta) it does not change: geansaí bán. L, n and r never take h: casóg liath.

ladder.en: At school, I wear a white shirt and grey trousers.
ladder.label: Bunúsach

ladder.ga: Ar scoil, caithim léine bhán[, geansaí dúghorm] agus bríste liath. [Sílim go bhfuil an éide compordach agus praiticiúil.]
ladder.en: At school, I wear a white shirt, a navy jumper and grey trousers. I think the uniform is comfortable and practical.
ladder.label: Níos fearr

ladder.ga: Ar scoil, caithim léine bhán, geansaí dúghorm agus bríste liath. Sílim go bhfuil an éide compordach agus praiticiúil[, ach caithfidh mé a rá go gcuireann an carbhat isteach orm. Ag an deireadh seachtaine, is fearr liom bríste géine agus T-léine a chaitheamh mar is maith liom a bheith compordach. An tseachtain seo caite, cheannaigh mé casóg dhearg san Iúr agus níor chosain sí ach fiche punt sa tsladmhargadh].
ladder.en: At school, I wear a white shirt, a navy jumper and grey trousers. I think the uniform is comfortable and practical, but I have to say that the tie annoys me. At the weekend, I prefer to wear jeans and a T-shirt because I like to be comfortable. Last week, I bought a red jacket in Newry and it only cost twenty pounds in the sale.
ladder.label: Is fearr

builders.title: Sláinte agus timpistí
builders.teaches: Talking about staying healthy (sport, food and sleep) and saying what is wrong; Tá ... orm for illnesses (tá slaghdán orm, tá tinneas cinn orm) and the question An bhfuil ... ort?; Tá mo ... nimhneach and Ghortaigh mé mo ... with mo + séimhiú (mo chos, mo ghlúin), no change on l, r or sc (mo lámh, mo rúitín, mo sceadamán) and m' before a vowel (m'uillinn); an injury at sport in the past (bhris mé, bhí orm dul); ag imirt + the genitive (ag imirt peile); advice with Ba chóir dom.

sprioc.ga: Tá mé ag foghlaim le labhairt faoi mo shláinte agus faoi bheith sláintiúil.
sprioc.en: I am learning to talk about my health and being healthy.

sprioc.ga: Tá mé ag foghlaim le rá cad é atá cearr liom agus cad é a tharla dom.
sprioc.en: I am learning to say what is wrong with me and what happened to me.

patterns.title: Tá ... orm
patterns.question: Cad é an focal beag a thaispeánann cé atá tinn? Cad é a tharlaíonn dó nuair a athraíonn an duine?
patterns.questionEn: Which little word tells you who is ill? What happens to it when the person changes?
patterns.rule: In Irish an illness is on you: Tá slaghdán orm (a cold is on me). The person is shown by ar: orm (me), ort (you), air (him), uirthi (her). Ask with An bhfuil ... ort? and answer Tá or Níl.
patterns.ruleEn: In Irish an illness is on you: Tá slaghdán orm (a cold is on me). The person is shown by ar: orm (me), ort (you), air (him), uirthi (her). Ask with An bhfuil ... ort? and answer Tá or Níl.

patterns.title: Ghortaigh mé mo ...
patterns.question: Cad é a tharlaíonn don fhocal i ndiaidh mo? Cad chuige nach n-athraíonn lámh ná rúitín?
patterns.questionEn: What happens to the word after mo? Why do lámh and rúitín not change?
patterns.rule: Mo puts a h after the first letter (séimhiú): mo chos, mo ghlúin. L, n and r never take h: mo lámh, mo rúitín. Sc, sm, sp and st do not take h either: mo sceadamán. Before a vowel, mo becomes m': m'uillinn.
patterns.ruleEn: Mo puts a h after the first letter (séimhiú): mo chos, mo ghlúin. L, n and r never take h: mo lámh, mo rúitín. Sc, sm, sp and st do not take h either: mo sceadamán. Before a vowel, mo becomes m': m'uillinn.

ladder.en: I broke my hand. I went to the doctor.
ladder.label: Bunúsach

ladder.ga: Bhris mé mo lámh [ag imirt peile Dé Sathairn seo caite]. Chuaigh mé chuig an dochtúir [san Iúr le mo mhamaí].
ladder.en: I broke my hand playing football last Saturday. I went to the doctor in Newry with my mum.
ladder.label: Níos fearr

ladder.ga: Bhris mé mo lámh ag imirt peile Dé Sathairn seo caite. Chuaigh mé chuig an dochtúir san Iúr le mo mhamaí. [Ar an drochuair, bhí orm scíth a ligean ar feadh seachtaine agus ní raibh cead agam peil a imirt ar feadh míosa. Caithfidh mé a rá gur chuir sé isteach go mór orm, ach beidh mé ar ais ar an fhoireann go luath.]
ladder.en: I broke my hand playing football last Saturday. I went to the doctor in Newry with my mum. Unfortunately, I had to rest for a week and I was not allowed to play football for a month. I have to say that it really annoyed me, but I will be back on the team soon.
ladder.label: Is fearr
